covers.title: The Box With Two Names
covers.prompt: A warm vertical children's storybook scene inside a magical lost-and-found shop: a thoughtful child with a blue coat holds a dented brass compass above an open wooden box containing two contradictory paper name tags, while the child's worried friend stands beside a sick parent's folded scarf and a kind shopkeeper listens without blaming either child. Soft golden light reveals tiny compass needles pointing toward two honest memories, a rain-dark window, and a small first-aid shelf in the background. Make the children, compass, and two labels the clear focal point; gentle tension, empathy, truth, and a safe hopeful resolution.

covers.title: The Last Seat at the Snow Table
covers.prompt: A bright vertical storybook illustration at a magical snow picnic: a child carrying two steaming mugs approaches a translucent ice table whose carved seats slowly rearrange, one place is marked for an absent friend, and three smaller newcomers stand nearby with empty hands. The child, ice table, and friends form a cooperative circle beneath paper lanterns and falling snow; a nearby empty sleigh and wide picnic blanket suggest a practical shared solution. Gentle blue and amber palette, expressive faces, cozy and fair, no villain and no written symbols.

covers.title: The Boy Who Stepped on the Painting
covers.prompt: A vertical children's museum storybook scene after a minor scuff: a boy kneels beside a large ornate landscape painting whose painted flowers softly glow, while a kind guide holds a silver repair case and a conservator approaches with a fine brush and gentle light. The boy looks honest and helpful as he cleans and supports the repair; the painting is damaged but recoverable, with no injury or danger. Warm gallery light, restorative rather than frightening, clear rounded forms, no written labels, letters, or text.

covers.title: The Birthday Where Two Cakes Were Enough
covers.prompt: A joyful vertical storybook party beneath a luminous willow at dusk: a thoughtful child host stands between two very different homemade cakes on a shared table, inviting a new family into the circle while an older baker reluctantly lowers a decorative cake tower. Children of different families exchange small gifts, an elderly neighbor receives a chair, and the two imperfect cakes become a balanced centerpiece. Warm paper lanterns, inclusive gestures, generous but not costless hospitality, expressive storybook characters, no text or decorations containing letters.

covers.title: The Promise Under the Rainbow
covers.prompt: A vertical children's fantasy adventure cover after rain: a child kneels beside an unfinished model bridge whose tiny rainbow arch is missing one glowing piece, while across a flooded garden the same child is seen helping a younger neighbor lift a basket to safety. A competition clock glows in the distance and the original promise is represented by a carefully kept ribbon, not text. Use the child, model bridge, helping hands, and rainbows as the visual story; hopeful integrity, changing plans, and keeping another promise.

covers.title: The Team Badge Without a Name
covers.prompt: A triumphant vertical fantasy sports storybook scene: a young runner holds a heavy gold relay badge with a blank central medallion while four diverse teammates gather around with a lantern, map roll, water flask, and repaired shoes. A small magical flame travels from each teammate's object into the badge, forming a shared ring rather than one winner's portrait. Celebratory stadium clouds, warm gold and teal palette, proud teamwork and fair credit, no letters, logos, numbers, or written text.

covers.title: The Captain Who Marked the Safe Route
covers.prompt: A vertical young-adult expedition fantasy cover on a high mountain bridge at sunrise: a young captain in a red weather coat holds a glowing map marker over a fork where a broad ceremonial road collapses into mist, while a shorter, quiet route specialist in a blue hood kneels beside carved trail symbols that prove the narrow path is safe. Pack animals and worried teammates wait behind them; a magical compass shows two competing light paths. Strong leadership, expertise, risk, and accountability, painterly realism, no lettering or map text.

covers.title: The Petition from the Other Side
covers.prompt: A vertical civic fantasy scene inside a packed old town hall divided by a newly proposed wall of pale stone: a young resident from the neighborhood behind the wall stands at a wooden speaking rail holding a model showing homes, wells, and a school cut off, while people on both sides listen with guarded expressions. A healer and shopkeeper offer practical testimony, the wall glows with competing magical protections, and the child faces the room rather than a villain. Emphasize genuine competing needs, public reasoning, and a nonviolent path forward, no readable documents or text.

covers.title: The Name on the Door
covers.prompt: A vertical community-hall fantasy cover at golden hour: a maintenance worker in overalls stands on a ladder beside a grand door bearing one oversized founder portrait, while children and neighbors carry repaired lamps, patched roof beams, jars of preserved seeds, and a hand-built stair rail toward a broad mosaic of many anonymous hands. A young organizer offers the worker a place beside the portrait rather than a token plaque. Warm workshop textures, recognition becoming responsibility, dignity, no written names or lettering.

covers.title: The Photograph Nobody Could Erase
covers.prompt: A vertical school newsroom fantasy scene: a student editor holds a magical camera whose latest luminous photograph reveals both a public official's lie and an innocent person's private fear, projected above a table of unprinted glass images. The editor stands between a demanding public advocate and a friend who does not want exposure, while a teacher considers confiscating the camera. Emphasize truth, privacy, evidence, and responsible publishing rather than punishment; thoughtful expressions, layered composition, no readable newspaper or written words.

covers.title: The Race Beside the Falling Wall
covers.prompt: A vertical fantasy race cover: young runners tear along a shortcut bridge beside an ancient city wall that is splitting into glowing blocks, while the safe course curves uphill behind them and homes with small children occupy the wall's shadow. One runner reaches the dangerous lever, another signals the neighborhood, and a judge raises an empty finish ribbon. Strong motion, fair competition, shared responsibility, visible consequence, adventurous rather than catastrophic, no readable signs or lettering.

covers.title: The Library Card for the River
covers.prompt: A vertical luminous library fantasy scene at the edge of town: a young librarian kneels beside a river flowing through the reading room in a clear ribbon, while the river's translucent presence carries lost story-reflections and reaches toward a blank catalog card on a wooden desk. Books from the river open with images instead of words, a child reads a shoreline memory, and a council clerk hesitates behind a ledger. Emphasize consent, rights, representation, and repair, welcoming wonder with ethical tension, no written text.

covers.title: The Helper Who Kept the Record
covers.prompt: A vertical school ethics fantasy cover inside an archive of suspended memory crystals: a student stands with a small proof shard raised toward a tall counselor whose office contains rows of glowing records, private memories, and one visibly duplicated crystal hidden in shadow. Classmates and a concerned teacher occupy different layers of the composition, some reassured and some disturbed. The student faces the system rather than a monster, emphasizing privacy, trust, evidence, and repair. Muted library blue, sharp crystal light, sophisticated realism, no written words.

covers.title: The Cure That Borrowed a Face
covers.prompt: A vertical magical medical ethics scene in a luminous healing chamber: a patient sits upright while a translucent healing spell forms a borrowed face and shared sensory ribbons between them, and an anxious family member reaches toward a consent crystal. A healer explains the cost through gesture; a mirror shows the patient's unchanged identity beneath the temporary features. The patient, overlapping faces, and family choice are the focal hierarchy. Serious, humane, non-graphic, sophisticated painterly fantasy, no text or medical labels.

covers.title: The Witness Who Signed the Treaty
covers.prompt: A vertical diplomatic fantasy cover inside a high treaty hall: the sole witness to a disputed border stands at a long table holding a pen above two overlapping maps, one showing villages and a river and another showing a different past. Delegations from both sides wait in tense silence, a wounded veteran watches, and magical boundary lines shift between truth and omission. The witness's conflicted expression and hand above the treaty are central. Mature political tension, restrained color, no readable writing, flags, logos, or text.

covers.title: The Prisoner Who Built the Library
covers.prompt: A vertical storybook prison-library scene connected to the outside world by an open arched doorway: an imprisoned architect carefully repairs a wooden bookcase while children and families from the town use the library beyond a guarded gate, proving its public value without erasing the consequences of her crime. A warden holds an unsigned pardon document represented by a folded blank paper, and the architect chooses with visible dignity. Warm lamplight against cool stone, justice, dependence, and repair, non-graphic, no text.

covers.title: The Map Drawn from Forgotten Names
covers.prompt: A vertical political-fantasy cover in a public mapping hall: a young cartographer draws glowing coastlines and village symbols back into a vast blank region of a living map while displaced homes, roads, and a broken bridge become visible beneath erased boundaries. Council maps show a neat prosperous city above, but damaged communities and a returning elder occupy the foreground. The cartographer's hand refuses a false border even as a senior official offers a silver compass. Emphasize material repair, representation, and consequences rather than symbolic gesture alone, no letters or labels.

covers.title: The City That Voted for Fear
covers.prompt: A vertical civic fantasy cover in a crowded council chamber after a magical attack: a young clerk stands before a great balance scale holding a glowing eye-shaped surveillance charm on one side and a small lantern of private citizen memories on the other. A frightened neighborhood watches from one balcony while a protest group stands with the lamp on the other, and a city warden's face shows uncertainty rather than malice. In the background, protective walls are being built. Sophisticated civic tension, humane faces, no villain, no written text.
